study.title: HAZOP – Hot DRI transfer conveyor and N2 fire protection (example)
study.unit: DRI plant – hot DRI transfer to EAF
study.scope: Hot DRI transfer from the reduction shaft discharge to the EAF hot-charging bin: enclosed belt conveyor, hood and gallery, dust extraction, and the N2 fire detection / inerting / extinguishing system that protects it.
study.exclusions: Reduction shaft furnace internals; EAF charging bin and EAF (covered by separate studies); plant N2 generation (air separation unit).
study.basis: Transfer hot DRI continuously in an enclosed conveyor to preserve heat and prevent re-oxidation and fire. DRI discharge temperature, belt temperature rating and N2 system design basis to be confirmed from the process design documents.
study.modes: Normal transfer, conveyor trip / stoppage under load, start-up after stoppage, shutdown and emptying, maintenance (hot work, belt change)

sessions.notes: Nodes N01 and N02 reviewed; N01 deviations on stoppage under load referred for quantification (R-001).

psi.title: Process design basis – DRI discharge temperature, conveyor and belt rating
Fire-protection design basis and cause & effect for the N2 system
Hot DRI / HBI handling hazards (self-heating, H2 generation with water) and N2 SDS

nodes.name: Hot DRI transfer conveyor – shaft discharge to EAF charging bin
nodes.batteryLimits: From the reduction shaft hot DRI discharge chute to the inlet of the EAF hot-charging bin, including the belt conveyor, drive, hood enclosure, gallery, dust extraction and emergency discharge chute
nodes.description: Transfer hot DRI continuously from the reduction shaft to the EAF charging bin in an enclosed conveyor, preserving its heat and preventing re-oxidation, self-heating and fire
nodes.designParams: Example: belt capacity 250 t/h; belt speed 2 m/s; enclosed hood with N2 inerting connection. DRI discharge temperature and belt temperature rating – to be confirmed from the design basis
nodes.operatingParams: Example: 150–200 t/h hot DRI; continuous operation; hood under slight negative pressure (dust extraction)
nodes.materials: Hot DRI / HBI and fines (self-heating, pyrophoric fines, H2 with water); combustible conveyor belt; CO from re-oxidation / combustion; N2 (asphyxiant)

nodes.name: N2 fire detection, inerting & extinguishing system for the conveyor
nodes.batteryLimits: From the plant N2 header isolation valve through the buffer vessel, pressure regulator PCV-211 and release valves XV-210A/B to the distribution header and nozzles in the conveyor hood; detection (SS-201, WT-201, LHD-201, GD-201A/B) and the extinguishing control panel
nodes.description: Detect a stoppage under load or a fire and flood the conveyor enclosure with N2 to prevent or extinguish a fire
nodes.designParams: Example: buffer vessel 10 barg; delivery to hood at regulated pressure; design discharge time per fire-protection design basis
nodes.operatingParams: Example: buffer vessel 6–8 barg; system on automatic; manual release from control room and local station

deviations.consequence: Conveyor stops under load: hot DRI stationary on the belt self-heats and re-oxidises; smouldering and belt fire; CO generation; fire may spread through the gallery to the transfer tower / DRI silo – potential fatality and extended outage
deviations.comments: Trips under load about 6 per year (plant records). Scenario quantified in the fault tree / event tree / bow tie examples.

deviations.consequence: Belt damage or ignition; smouldering DRI carried to the EAF charging bin; conveyor fire
deviations.comments: N2 system not claimed as IPL here – already credited for the stoppage scenario and shares the detection.

deviations.consequence: Water on hot DRI generates heat and hydrogen; air ingress re-oxidises the DRI – fire or hydrogen explosion inside the hood
DRI fines accumulate in the enclosure and gallery and re-oxidise; smouldering fire; dust ignition during hot work
N2 not delivered to the conveyor enclosure on demand – a fire after a stoppage under load is not prevented or extinguished; escalation to a major gallery fire
deviations.comments: Dominant contributors in the fault tree example (gate G-002): enclosure not sealed, PCV-211 fails closed, nozzles blocked, isolation valve left closed.

deviations.consequence: N2 buffer inventory low or lost – system cannot inert / extinguish when demanded
Personnel enter the hood or gallery during or soon after an N2 release (or a leak) – asphyxiation, potential fatality
deviations.comments: Hazard introduced by the protection system itself (see the bow tie example).

causes.text: [S] Conveyor, feeder or vibratory feeder stopped (belt tear, drive trip, chute blockage)
Power failure; instrument air failure (valves go to fail position)
Pull-cord or belt-drift trip; EAF charging bin full / downstream blockage
Re-oxidation in air (insufficient inerting or cooling)
Conveyor or transport vessel over-temperature
Reduction / cooling upset – over-temperature DRI discharged onto the belt
Ingress of air, water or lubricant
Rain ingress through a damaged hood or open inspection doors
[S] Oxygen or air ingress into reducing gas or inerted systems
Dust accumulation on structures; poor housekeeping
Hot surfaces, sparks, static, hot work
Equipment failure – control valve fails closed, isolation valve, pump or compressor trip, vessel failure
Blockage, gas lock or vapour lock
Both N2 release valves XV-210A/B fail to open (common cause)
Distribution header / nozzles blocked by DRI fines
Isolation in error (wrong valve closed, LOTO on wrong equipment)
Failure of steam / nitrogen / cooling water
Failure of hydraulic power / electric power
Leak or purge into enclosed or confined area
Pit, tunnel or bin atmosphere not tested before entry

safeguards.description: Restart / emergency discharge of hot DRI within safe time (procedure + discharge chute)
N2 fire detection & inerting / extinguishing system – auto-initiated on stoppage under load or fire detection
Manual fire fighting (hydrants / monitors) by the emergency response team
Fire separation of the conveyor gallery (fire breaks / dampers)
DRI discharge high-high temperature trip – stops feed onto the conveyor
High DRI temperature alarm with operator response
Hood inspection rounds and inspection-door position monitoring
Dust extraction from the conveyor hood
Six-monthly function and blow-through test of the N2 system
Low N2 buffer pressure alarm with operator response
N2 isolation valve locked open; line-up check after maintenance
N2 release warning beacons and enclosure access lock-out
O2 monitoring and confined-space entry permit for the hood / gallery

recs.text: Quantify the PFDavg of the N2 system (XS-210) by fault tree and the fire escalation by event tree; confirm the required risk reduction (see the fault tree / event tree examples).
Make the emergency discharge chute operable without power (or put the drive control on UPS) so hot DRI can be cleared after a power failure.
Review the fire separation of the gallery to the transfer tower / DRI silo; the fire-spread scenario is above the tolerable frequency.
Confirm the design DRI discharge temperature and the belt material temperature rating – the values in the project documents differ.
Install inspection-door position switches with alarm in the control room; review the need for H2 detection in the hood.
Add the N2 delivery path (release valves, PCV-211, nozzles) to the FMECA and the proof-test plan; consider a redundant pressure regulator.
Lock out access to the conveyor enclosure during and after an N2 release; require an O2 check before entry.
